# Native edition first study

The [hierarchical consumer history](hierarchy-consumer-first.json.gz) retains
13 records: the P1 review, original sources, actual diagnostic failure and a
separate passing malformed-obligation test whose legacy header masked payload
coverage. Two failed current-frame/context repair attempts remain distinct.
The active stand-ins now use native-result 3. Malformed obligation reports
must pass the current context check before their intended payload refusal;
the conditional reconstruction refusal remains required as well. The actual
small native instrument controls check both APIs and finite-leaf reconstruction.
Both Rust versions pass the two diagnostic and three selected instrument tests
and strict target Clippy; the other hierarchy cases are not credited here.
The bounded passive reader pins all 353,780 expanded bytes and never executes
saved observers, packets or commands. Transient generated files were not
separately retained; their complete authored literals remain in the originals.
Current-head CI/review and broader proof/release gates remain open.

The separate [protocol consumer history](consumer-protocol-first.json.gz)
retains eight original source/observer/result records, including both complete
hosted diagnostic-test failures and two actual local pre-repair failures.
The diagnostic checker stand-in still replied in the old protocol; the direct
rectangular pure-leaf test still framed its requests as QLV2. Current consumers
now use native-result 3 and explicit edition-2026 QLV3, retaining the same
refusal categories, text/JSON checks and independent malformed-request cases.
Both actual Rust versions pass all 18 existing tests and strict target Clippy.
Transient generated project/checker files were not separately retained; their
complete authored literals remain in the original test sources. The bounded
reader pins all 271,530 expanded bytes without executing saved code or packets.
Production checks, historical fixtures and work/size limits are unchanged;
new-head CI/review and broader proof/release gates remain open.

The separate [capacity consumer history](consumer-capacity-first.json.gz)
preserves the original test/helper/manifest, actual macOS CI failure and local
reproduction before correcting the aggregate-byte oracle. Retained manifest
bytes now count alongside local and bundled sources in the existing test;
production limits and exact-boundary/one-byte-under checks are unchanged.
Normal/MSRV runs pass all four existing capacity tests and strict Clippy.
An initially canceled command with incomplete environment selection remains
separate from those results. The archive is inert; full current-head CI and
broader proof/release gates remain open.

The later [consumer validation history](consumer-validation-first.json.gz)
retains 23 original source/diagnostic records and three explicitly derived
context summaries (532,293 expanded archive bytes; SHA-256
`cefe8d9c6a2637892c4899a3c28422a9154e5541bce51ecb8f06fb4167642734`).
Complete repetitive routine source-hash inventories stay private; exact source
commits, source-window digests and unrelated dirty-file identities remain bound.
It separates qargo's missing-Edition compile errors, a Clippy invocation that
lost its local source override, and exact-head PR #423 Rustdoc/CLI/foreign
consumer failures. Hosted temporary input/artifact files were not collected;
the original consumer sources and full returned logs are retained. The passive
reader never executes history. Current native checks, full CI, packaging and
installation remain separate from this record and from Issue completion.
The separate [observer failures](consumer-observer-first.json.gz) retain seven
records (39,941 expanded bytes; SHA-256
`5a08506e3160bd169f55210b4fd7433dbdf0bd0f389eb4d398b2b446756414cc`).
An incomplete Python validator environment and a passive reader's incorrect
assumption about saved tool wrappers remain distinct from product failures.

This informed manual study precedes implementation of [#255](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/issues/255)
and the related [edition/release boundary #137](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/issues/137).
No external model was invoked. The immutable [archive](first.json.gz) preserves
791 original files, 1,566,434 expanded source/log bytes, including the unchanged
757-member `SESSION.pending.json` and 33 later native-study records. The old
index's pending status remains historical; it is not rewritten into approval.

The archive has SHA-256
`80df6cba3f022d8b2aafe4824c468d034309d100f61e5cbbc784b83f6e11483b`.
Gzip and base64 are storage only. The fixed integrity reader hashes and decodes
in memory, verifies every original byte/mode and index member, and never runs
captured scripts, commands, binaries or packets.

- Attempt 01 used unsupported `--json` in all ten commands. These usage
  refusals establish no source-edition or native behavior.
- Attempt 02 corrects only the CLI option to `--format=json`. Seven manifest
  problems reject before native invocation; explicit 2026 initialization
  succeeds with 76 recorded native calls. The scalar's quantum-valued `main`
  separately gives `invalid_entry`; its diagnostic exists, but an assertion
  interrupted separate per-case command metadata retention.
- Attempt 03 changes that function name to a library declaration. Scalar
  checking succeeds with 76 native calls; a nested 2027 manifest rejects before
  native invocation. First sources and failures remain separate from repairs.
- The thirteen-mode inventory is a static reading of the original Main source.
  Only seven native queries on the existing one-bit ordinary identity were run:
  QLV2 accepts, wrong product rejects, proposed QLV3 editions 2026/2027/0 all
  reject as `format`, and an external QLV1 or trailing QLV2 also rejects.

The actual old QLV2 header and native response lack requested-edition context.
This records the missing implementation; it is not a native edition proof.
The observed head is `c6a95e8488ad44bc398f9cfa97def807058436e5`.
Captured source windows and CLI/kernel digests identify the observed prior
bytes, not a fresh clean build or compiler/runtime preservation theorem.
The two direct local windows (1.601 and 1.583 seconds) are not CI benchmarks.

No QLV3 implementation, new accepted API, general QLT, maximum-size quantum
case, new guarantee, Issue completion or release is claimed. The existing two
scoped QLV1 guarantees and broader pending QS/PR/RS/EXACT duties remain.

The [native/Rust integration record](native-context-integration-first.json.gz),
SHA-256 `e5ac7bbfe3c03d951e57879ad668f29585e5233cb4a8b96bb22f1c56500b16fb`,
retains 113 records (2,204,865 expanded archive bytes). Prototype Lean proof
failures, first Rust API compilation failures and two stale negative-frame
mutations remain distinct from later checks. Thirteen small CLI observations
retain actual source/manifest bytes and local binary/input windows. The first
component counterexample accidentally changed both request and actual through
shared Python objects; its two accepts remain intact. Eight separate corrected
calls use independent copies, retain the actual unchanged packet and reject
changed requests, unsupported editions and wrong scope. The initial component
heredoc and outer assertion traceback were observed but not captured as files;
this archive makes no complete-harness claim. It is inert history, never a
current test/proof result or #255 completion. Routine normal/MSRV validation
logs remain outside fixtures; current-evidence continuity and full CI are pending.

The [first helper diagnostics](native-helper-first.json.gz), SHA-256
`aea25ce49107d31122f240b72937bd96189e4d27ebaae5bf0d2a0ada631ba50b`,
retain 19 records (19,229 expanded archive bytes). They preserve the old QLV2
helper's actual rejection, an unsupported CLI harness argument, four missing-
edition invocation failures, and the production source-inventory refusal.
Two separate QLV3 hierarchy requests retain the real diagnostic regression:
noncanonical finite descriptions reported `invalid_ir` instead of the existing
`format` classification. The repair preserves the original oracle and delegates
error projection to the existing hierarchy classifier; it changes no acceptance.
Four original committed sources are bound by exact Git references at
`d38d27c0d37dd658441e53e53da7f341cd1dc608`, including the observed native source.
The intermediate SourceKernel helper's full preimage and child CLI streams were
not captured; its actual harness failure remains distinct from later successful
checks. The passive reader never executes saved code or packets. This history
does not establish current CI, continuity, proof discharge or #255 completion.

The [first Python context study](python-context-first.json.gz), SHA-256
`762f4872db96fb3c4380549402af59d63a90043c7d0375ab35833c02640a7616`,
retains 32 records (47,993 expanded archive bytes): one-bit desired Python,
QLI and QASM sources, the observer, and five observations in each environment.
The desired explicit constructor was absent; the new source-expectation flag
was unsupported. The first sandbox run could not execute `ps` for descendant
cleanup and obscured the raw-client result. A separately authorized unrestricted
run retains the actual missing-edition diagnostic. Both first histories stay
intact, including the successful ordinary manifest-based source emission.
Four committed implementation sources are bound at
`0e4fd2601d187a674f8865fd8729f05e2a462b19`; observed prior binary digests are
not fresh build attestation. Passive byte checking executes no saved observer,
program or packet, and supplies no current acceptance or preservation proof.
